_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Mathematics Standard (041), set 30/1/3 (Series GE1FH, SET-3). 27 pages: idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English instructions + Q1; English on EVERY EVEN index 2-26, Hindi on every odd index 1-25 (each odd page is the Hindi of the page after it). The tops of all odd pages were checked on the contact sheet and open with Hindi; the last page (idx 26) is English. No parity inversion. Instruction (viii) prints the internal-choice count: 2 in B, 2 in C, 2 in D, 3 in E = 9 alternatives, all found on the paper and confirmed against a bare OR in the marking scheme (Q21, Q22, Q28, Q30, Q32, Q35, Q36, Q37, Q38). Decimal points on this paper are RAISED (Q1, Q10, Q36), written 1{\cdot}73. All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the marking scheme for 30/1/3; each was also re-derived and agrees. Sibling of 30/1/1: 42 rows confirmed on this paper's pages and copied byte-for-byte from 2025-30-1-1 (stem, context, options, answer, chapter, subtopic, difficulty), 11 rows new (Q1, Q2, Q11, Q16, Q17, Q18, Q25, Q26, Q27, Q33, Q34). Every _figure was read on this paper's own pages. Case studies are reordered: this paper's Case Study 1 (lighthouse) is 30/1/1's Case Study 3, Case Study 2 (charity run) is 30/1/1's Case Study 1, Case Study 3 (brooch) is 30/1/1's Case Study 2.

questions.context: Questions number 19 and 20 are Assertion and Reason based questions. Two statements are given, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.
questions.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The probability of selecting a number at random from the numbers 1 to 20 is 1.

**Reason (R) :** For any event E, if P(E) = 1, then E is called a sure event.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.context:
A school is organizing a charity run to raise funds for a local hospital. The run is planned as a series of rounds around a track, with each round being 300 metres. To make the event more challenging and engaging, the organizers decide to increase the distance of each subsequent round by 50 metres. For example, the second round will be 350 metres, the third round will be 400 metres and so on. The total number of rounds planned is 10.

Based on the information given above, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: Write the fourth, fifth and sixth term of the Arithmetic Progression so formed.
